key_insight: This survey uses world modeling to connect video understanding and video generation: both work with videos that reveal only partial, imperfect views of an evolving world.
problem_solved: Video foundation models and video world models are often studied separately despite their shared need to relate visible sequences to underlying world dynamics. The survey offers a unified perspective on these developments.
method: Adopt world modeling as a common lens for examining video foundation models and video world models.
Treat video as a partial, lossy, temporally ordered projection of a latent world.
Compare the objectives of understanding and generating video with those of modeling underlying world dynamics.
impact: This perspective can help AI/ML practitioners distinguish modeling visible video patterns from modeling the world processes behind them. It also provides a conceptual bridge between video understanding, generation, and world modeling.
visual_elements: Latent-world-to-video diagram showing an evolving world projected into partially observed video frames.
Two converging paths labeled 'Video foundation models' and 'Video world models,' meeting at a shared world-modeling lens.
Timeline contrasting visible frames with hidden states and unobserved events.
Four icons representing the title’s themes: reading, writing, sharing, and interacting through video.
paper_title: Reading, Writing, Sharing, and Interacting with the World through Video
paper_authors: Shengqiong Wu, Meng Luo, Bobo Li, Ziwei Liu, Shuicheng Yan
